payload.rationale: The binding condition is an unsmoothed GISS LOTI annual 2026 value above 1.28 C (2025 at 1.19 is easily cleared). Jan–Aug 2026 average 1.224 C (sum 9.79). To reach a reported 1.29 C, Sep–Dec must average about 1.41–1.42 C (roughly 1.41 if 1.285 rounds up). That is at or above the exceptional late-2023 El Niño months (Sep–Dec 2023 averaged ~1.41 C), so the year needs a record-warm final third. Supporting this: August 2026 at 1.40 C is a very large jump from July (1.25) and far above prior Augusts, consistent with strong warming momentum and possibly a developing El Niño, whose global-temperature effect typically builds through late year. Monthly anomalies are autocorrelated, so a Sep–Dec mean near 1.35–1.45 is plausible; my central estimate is roughly 1.38 with ~0.08 C spread on the four-month mean, giving roughly a one-in-three chance of clearing the bar. Reasons this may be too low: if a strong El Niño is underway, late-2026 months could run 1.45–1.55 C as in 2023–24, making 1.29+ likely; upward revisions to earlier months could also help. Reasons this may be too high: the August spike may be transient (single-month noise), ENSO may be neutral or weak, and the required Sep–Dec average would be a record for those months; even a strong finish averaging 1.38 falls short. No ENSO state or forecast was supplied, so the key driver is uncertain.
limitations: No ENSO forecast or current ENSO state supplied; the estimate relies on persistence of the August anomaly and general background.
Four months of 2026 data missing; GISS monthly values are subject to revision.
Rounding/tie handling at exactly 1.28 C is uncertain; assumed a reported value of 1.29 or higher is needed.
Packet annual 2025 value (1.19) may differ from other reported figures; used as supplied.
No fitted statistical model; judgment-based estimate.
